findings.explanation: The slice end was changed from `(index + 1) * size` (equivalent to `index * size + size`) to `index * size + size - 1`. This drops the last element of every page: e.g. page(['a','b','c','d','e','f'], 0, 3) now returns ['a','b'] instead of ['a','b','c']. Every caller of this pagination helper will silently receive one fewer item per page than requested.
findings.suggestedComment: This introduces an off-by-one: the slice end is now `size - 1` short, so each page returns one fewer item than `size` (e.g. page(items,0,3) yields 2 items instead of 3). Should this go back to `index*size + size` (or `(index+1)*size`)?

findings.explanation: SEND-14 asks for up to three retries with exponential backoff. This implementation makes exactly one retry attempt (the single `call()` in the catch block) with no delay or backoff logic at all, so it stops far short of the three-attempt, backed-off policy the ticket describes.
findings.suggestedComment: This only retries once with no delay, but SEND-14 calls for up to three attempts with exponential backoff. Can you add a retry loop/counter and a backoff delay between attempts?

findings.explanation: The bare `catch {}` discards the original error entirely rather than capturing it. If the retry in line 5 also rejects, the caller sees that second rejection, not the original error the requirement says to give up with — the first failure's information (message, stack, cause) is lost.
findings.suggestedComment: The original error is dropped here (`catch {}`), so if the retry also fails the caller only ever sees the second error, not the original one SEND-14 says to surface. Capture the first error and rethrow/attach it when retries are exhausted.
